name: Bernie Sanders
role: U.S. senator from Vermont (2007-present); candidate for the Democratic presidential nomination (2016, 2020)
summary: Self-described democratic socialist who favors single-payer health care, tuition-free public college, a higher minimum wage, high taxes on wealth, strong unions and worker ownership, and large public climate investment. He opposes most trade deals, the Iraq war and mass surveillance, backs a two-state solution while pressing to cut arms sales to Israel, and rejects open borders while supporting a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Says he will never hesitate to defend the nation and has backed veterans and defence of allies.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Wants to cut the prison population by half and reform and demilitarise police, while saying officers deserve respect; does not call for abolition.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted against amendments to bar federal funds for groups that perform or promote abortion and voted to table a ban on federal abortion funding in the 2009 health bill.

ban-cartels.rationale: His 2020 plan breaks up monopolies and corrupt mergers.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Plan includes majority sign-up, first-contract arbitration and public-sector bargaining rights.

collective-defense.rationale: Praises NATO as 'collective defense against a common enemy' and wants a similar organisation against violent extremism.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Names consumerism, with greed and oligarchy, as part of the current path the country must leave.

corporate-influence.rationale: Says Wall Street's lobbying and campaign money corrupt the political system and calls for public funding of elections.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Plan commits to rooting out institutional racism and addressing racial disparities in wealth, health, housing and justice.

death-penalty.rationale: His criminal justice plan abolishes the death penalty, and Our Revolution lists its abolition among the platform's goals.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Adopts FDR's Second Bill of Rights, which includes guaranteed economic rights to health care, housing and a decent job.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Plan calls for 100% renewable electricity and transport by 2030 and decarbonisation by 2050, $16 trillion in public investment.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Wants to expand on NATO-style collective defence for the 21st century and backs allies against Russia; also wants troops home from endless wars.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: His Green New Deal plan transforms the energy system away from fossil fuels.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Green New Deal plan would stop building new nuclear plants and impose a moratorium on license renewals.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Our Revolution proposes a financial transaction tax of 0.5 percent on stock trades, 0.1 percent on bonds and 0.005 percent on derivatives.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Calls for a fair and progressive tax code and attacks tax breaks for the rich, the opposite of a single flat rate.

free-public-college.rationale: Wrote the College for All Act and says every qualified person should be able to attend public college tuition-free.

free-trade.rationale: Voted against NAFTA in 1993 and against the USMCA in 2020, and voted for a 2015 amendment requiring congressional approval before more countries join the TPP.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: His platform commits to rooting out institutional racism and discrimination.

future-generations.rationale: Says our responsibility is to leave the planet habitable for children and grandchildren.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: Our Revolution says the scientific community is absolutely clear that climate change is caused by human activity, mainly burning fossil fuels.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said in 2015 that Israel has a right to exist and in 2024 that it had a right to respond to October 7, but in 2025 said Gaza is a genocide.

job-guarantee.rationale: In It's OK to Be Angry About Capitalism he says that in 2020 he proposed a federal jobs guarantee establishing that every American has a right to a job.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Says Citizens United must be overturned and elections publicly funded because billionaire campaign money corrupts democracy.

limit-guns.rationale: His 2020 plan bans assault weapons and high-capacity magazines and requires universal background checks, but does not seek to prohibit gun ownership in general.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Green New Deal plan limits federal funding to publicly owned drinking-water utilities and favours public and cooperative utilities and broadband.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Plan abolishes three-strikes laws and mandatory minimum sentences.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Says he believes in private companies that invest and grow and rejects government ownership of the means of production, but also rejects 'unfettered capitalism' and backs large public programs.

nation-first.rationale: Says unilateral action should be a last resort and wants a coalition including NATO partners, Russia and the Arab League, though he puts rebuilding America first.

national-self-determination.rationale: Says Palestinians deserve a state of their own and that Ukraine's sovereignty must be defended.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Adopts FDR's Second Bill of Rights, with guaranteed economic rights including health care, housing and jobs.

no-bailouts.rationale: He voted for an amendment to end $272 billion of TARP bailout spending (2009), but his record on rescuing failing firms in general is mixed.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Says he fought for decades against corporate welfare and an unfair tax system and walked picket lines against deals such as NAFTA.

open-borders.rationale: Asked in 2015 about open borders: 'No, that's a Koch brothers proposal'; says it would make Americans poorer.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Voted against the 1993 Skelton amendment that wrote 'Don't ask, don't tell' into law, in two separate votes.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Supports workplace democracy, with worker-elected boards and cooperatives.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Frames his politics as 'American idealism' and rebuilding the country for working families.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Calls the political system 'in many respects, corrupt' because of money and lobbying.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Our Revolution calls for putting a price on carbon, alongside transforming the energy system, so it is one tool among several.

positive-liberty.rationale: Adopts FDR's view that true freedom requires economic security and says people are not free when they cannot feed their families or get health care.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Says Americans have a free press, but that to a significant degree the oligarchs own that media, so it rarely asks embarrassing questions.

public-ownership.rationale: His 2019 Green New Deal plan puts new renewable power under public ownership through federal power authorities and public utilities, but his 2015 Georgetown speech says he does not want government to own the means of production.

public-service-media.rationale: Calls for a significant investment in public media and cites research tying secure, independent public media funding to healthy democracies.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Says racial disparities and institutional racism remain, with five types of violence against Black and brown Americans.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In Our Revolution he calls the $7.25 minimum wage a starvation wage that must become a living wage, raised to $15 an hour.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His platform welcomes refugees and a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants but keeps limits on legal admission rather than open entry.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Plan to break up monopolies and mergers, ban stock buybacks, require federal charters for large firms and put workers on boards.

rehabilitation.rationale: His criminal justice plan moves away from an overly punitive approach toward rehabilitating people who have made mistakes.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Plan bans permanent replacement of strikers, gives federal workers the right to strike and bars mandatory anti-union meetings.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Says rich countries have a moral responsibility to address international poverty, and his climate plan funds the Green Climate Fund.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted against the 1996 Defense of Marriage Act on passage and for the amendment to suspend its federal definition of marriage.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Plan would mandate criminal liability for police civil-rights violations, end qualified immunity limits and require investigation of killings in custody.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: Our Revolution lists closing loopholes that let multinationals avoid taxes by stashing cash in offshore tax havens, and he later introduced a bill barring profit-sheltering in tax havens.

social-market-economy.rationale: Wants private companies to thrive alongside universal social protection and anti-monopoly rules.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: Our Revolution announces a U.S. Employee Ownership Bank to give low-interest loans, grants and technical help to workers buying their businesses.

state-harmful.rationale: His platform expands the role of government (single-payer, public college, jobs programs) and says government belongs to all of us.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Platform: cancel all student debt for about 45 million Americans.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted against the House reauthorizations of the USA PATRIOT Act in 2005 and 2006 and against the 2011 Senate extension.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: His signature programs are universal (tuition-free college for all, Medicare for All) rather than limited to the poorest.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Our Revolution calls a stronger estate tax one of the fairest ways to reduce wealth inequality and raise revenue.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Calls for the wealthiest and the largest corporations to pay their fair share, and criticises billionaires for rigging the tax code.

taxation-theft.rationale: Argues the wealthy and corporations must pay their fair share to fund public programs.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Voted for the 2015 amendment to reaffirm the prohibition on torture.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Our Revolution says strong and binding labor, environmental and human rights standards must be written into the core text of all trade agreements.

unions-good.rationale: Says the trade union movement built the middle class and set a goal of doubling union membership.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He wrote the Medicare for All Act of 2023 (S. 1655), which covers every U.S. resident with a single public program.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Says a power structure protects extreme wealth inequality, that billionaires buy elections and that this is an oligarchy.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Plan rescinds the 'public charge' rule so immigrants can use basic supports, and college-for-all applies regardless of immigration status.

worker-ownership.rationale: Our Revolution proposes aid for workers who want to buy their own businesses and praises worker cooperatives, and his 2020 plan has large firms transfer 20% of ownership to workers; it is support for worker ownership, not a call for all firms to be owned this way.

workplace-democracy.rationale: His 2020 plan has workers directly elect 45% of the board of large corporations.

notes: Platform pages are archived copies of his 2020 campaign site. Later pass 2026-11-18 (rules 7): the three Sanders books in the local library (Our Revolution, Where We Go from Here, It's OK to Be Angry About Capitalism) and Voteview roll calls are now read; answers that rested on Wikipedia summaries were re-sourced to them or nulled. His views on Israel have shifted: he affirmed Israel's right to exist (2015) and supported its response to October 7 (2024), then called Gaza a genocide and said he is not a Zionist (2025). The 1970s-80s public-ownership statements are older than his 2015 'government should not own the means of production' line. Themes searched in the books and votes: health care, wages, taxes, trade, climate, energy, criminal justice, guns, immigration, civil liberties, LGBT rights, abortion, war and alliances, Israel, unions, ownership, campaign finance, media. Most statements about ideology, religion, ethnicity, monarchy and similar topics are never addressed by him and stay null.
